subject: art-design
title: Critical Analysis Terms: Application
welcome_lead: Move into spatial terms — foreground, juxtaposition, motif — and apply them.
meta_desc: Applying GCSE analysis terms: foreground, juxtaposition, motif, symbolism.
final_note: Spatial and conceptual terms together make analysis precise.

concepts.def: The front area closest to the viewer.
Middle distance between front and back.
The area furthest from the viewer.
Placing two things side by side for contrast.
Object that stands for an idea or belief.

walkthroughs.body_html: Use foreground, middleground, background to walk an examiner through an image. "In the foreground a child kneels; in the middleground a fence; the background fades into mist." This shows you understand spatial composition.

Juxtaposition sets two contrasting elements side by side to spark meaning. A skull next to fresh flowers in a still life juxtaposes life and death. Always state what is juxtaposed and what effect it creates.

A motif is a visual element repeated through a work or body of work — Frida Kahlo's heart motif, for instance. Symbolism means an object standing for something else — a candle for hope, a chain for restriction.
